message.content:
Quantum entanglement is when two particles become linked so that measuring one instantly tells you something about the other, no matter how far apart they are.

A simple analogy: imagine two special coins that are “entangled.” If you flip one and it lands heads, you immediately know the other is tails. The strange part in quantum physics is that before you look, neither coin has a definite result yet — but when you check one, the other’s state is connected to it.
